question: What amplitude-free direction and load-response restrictions follow from the published first-star PES plus equal passive relaxation?
assumptions: three equal independent passive Debye channels coupled to published rigid first-star Fourier waves
same participating contact and dissipative force estimator at both directions
axis registration and phase/cycle averaging; C>0
physical_mapping: physical time and length in assumed bath; tau=eta/kappa is not graphite-measured; UD material source/loss still OPEN
target_exposure: Known paired 21.8/38.2 peaks and weak load dependence; the direction-ratio formula is derived after that exposure from an existing conventional null
fitted_choices: none in exact ratio; choosing equal channels is an assumed restricted model
sources: Lebedeva et al. arXiv:2511.01338v1 Eq. 2 and Table 4
Chen et al. PRL 137, 166201 (2026) public abstract
UD-Physics graphite-2d-relaxation exact receipt at base a7c6b12
baseline: Conventional three-wave passive bath; compare to measured direction-resolved dissipated power, not static PES coefficient
result: R(x)=(x+2)(3x+4)/[2(x+1)(x+4)] strictly increases 1 to 3/2 for x>0; pressure slope 2K(x)(d ln g + d ln tau); shared-tau N13/N7 horizontal collapse.
next_discriminant: Measure registered direction-resolved, velocity-odd dissipated power and independent linewidth at N7; reserve speeds/pressures for held-out test; measure N13 if detection allows.
